title: The factor-2 integrality-gap conjecture for the ATSP subtour LP
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: For every directed metric, is the minimum Hamiltonian-tour cost at most twice the optimum of the standard subtour-elimination linear program?
context:
Distinct from the undirected 4/3 conjecture; these are the two classical TSP relaxation barriers.

sentences: Asymmetric travelling salesman seeks a cheapest directed tour through all vertices of a directed metric.
The source proposal asks whether its optimum is always at most twice the standard subtour LP optimum.
That relaxation buys fractional arcs while requiring the degree and cut conditions necessary for a tour.
A factor-two theorem would identify a central limit of this widely used approach to directed routing.
This is a statement about the relaxation's integrality gap, and the saved proposal still lacks the full model and progress discussion needed for a finished card.
